title: The night black came up 26 times

probes.question: True or false: after many blacks in a row, red becomes more likely on the next roulette spin.
What is the belief that a long streak must soon reverse called?

image.alt: Close-up of a casino roulette wheel with red and black numbered pockets and a white ball near the zero

panels.text: Monte Carlo, August 1913. At a casino roulette table, the ball lands on black. Then black again. And again.
Gamblers start betting on red: surely a run this long has to end soon.
Black keeps coming. The ball lands on black 26 times in a row, and the gamblers lose millions of francs betting against it.
The twist: the wheel has no memory. Each spin is independent, so a long run of black does not make red more likely. The mistake is now called the gambler's fallacy.
